title: How Taiwan’s November Local Elections Could Change the World - The Wire China
gist: Taiwan's November 28 local elections, in which the DPP could win KMT strongholds Taipei and New Taipei, will shape the 2028 presidential race, which is likely to pit President Lai Ching-te against Taichung mayor Lu Shiow-yen. The authors argue that a DPP surge would raise the odds of Beijing escalating economic or military coercion, and that the China Coast Guard is already rehearsing the steps of a quarantine or soft blockade.

themes.theme: Taipei and New Taipei races as bellwethers

insights.claim: The DPP is overperforming in the KMT strongholds of Taipei City and New Taipei City, which it last won in 1994 and 2001 respectively, and could win both in the same election.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Winning both cities would be a historic shift and a clear sign of DPP strength going into 2028.
insights.quote: It could now win both in the same election, giving Lai’s re-election prospects a substantial boost.

insights.claim: DPP Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen, founder of the civil defense group Kuma Academy, has narrowed his poll deficit to 1.2 percent behind incumbent Chiang Wan-an as of September 22, after earlier being projected to lose in a landslide.

insights.so_what: The Taipei race is a toss-up, and a Shen win would elevate a politician Beijing regards as a hard-line separatist.
